maps.title: Gita Week — the teaching in one map

nodeData.topic: Gita Week — the teaching in one map
nodeData.note: Sri Gauranga Das's 7-day overview of the Bhagavad-gita As It Is, arranged by his own frame: why read it, Arjuna's crisis, the five truths (soul, work, the Lord, nature and the modes, time), the mind, knowledge and the guru, and devotion as the essence. Every bubble is a moment from the classes with its minute and a verbatim line; the link plays it. Tap Orbit for 3D; the story 'The Gita in 12 steps' is ready under ⋯ → Stories.

children.topic: Why read the Gita
The Gita is like an ocean
children.note: Like the ocean off Durban's beach, the Gita gets deeper the further you go in. Seven days can only be a brief overview, not an in-depth study. — "the Gita is like an ocean. You have a nice beach here in Durban, right? And so the ocean is very deep."

children.topic: Spoken by Krishna to Arjuna at Kurukshetra
children.note: The audience recalls the basics: Krishna spoke the Gita to Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra, 5,000 years ago. — "I'm just trying to remember who actually spoke the Gita. Can anyone help me with that? Krishna. Lord Krishna."

children.topic: The Gita is alive
children.note: The one truly unique feature: the Gita gives fresh meaning every time you open it, at whatever level you are. — "But there is one very unique characteristic of the Gita and that is the Gita is alive."

children.topic: Gandhi: fresh joy from it every day
children.note: Gandhi's words from the book's back cover: when doubts and disappointments come, he found comfort in the Gita and new meaning daily. — "I turn to the Bhagat Gita and find your words to comfort me. And I immediately begin to smile in the midst of overwhelming sorrow."

children.topic: Open any page and find your answer
children.note: When something is bothering you, open the Gita anywhere and the answer will be there. — "open the Gita. Any page, anyhow. Not that you have to go to a specific chapter, you have to go to a specific page. No, just open it and you will actually find that the answer you're seeking is in those pages."

children.topic: Gita Mahatmya: why read the Gita
children.note: Prabhupada includes Shankaracharya's verses on the glories of the Gita; these give the reasons to read it. — "Shankar Achara was a great acharia for the adita school and he wrote on the Bhagat Gita. He wrote about the glories of the Gita."

children.topic: Choosing soap: why choose this book
children.note: Just as we pick soap by quality, fragrance and ingredients, the Mahatmya tells us the qualities that make the Gita worth choosing. — "Let's say you're buying some soap and then you have a whole bunch of options. There's many many types of soaps."

children.topic: Context is war, content is life
children.note: Though spoken on a battlefield, the Gita is about how to live, not about warfare. — "So the context is war but the content is life. It's all about life. It's not about war."

children.topic: Freedom from fear and lamentation
children.note: Mahatmya verse 1: following the Gita frees one from bhaya (fear) and shoka (lamentation) now, and gives a spiritual next life. — "If one properly follows the instructions of how to one can be free from all miseries and anxieties in this life and one's next life will be spiritual."

children.topic: Two kinds of punya: material and spiritual
children.note: Material piety takes you to heavenly planets; spiritual piety takes you out of the material world altogether. — "There is material puna and spiritual puna. So material puna puna means pious activities."

children.topic: Gita is the milk of the Vedas
children.note: Mahatmya verse 6: the Upanishads are the cow, Krishna the milker, Arjuna the calf, and the Gita is the milk for devotees to drink. — "Just like if the if you if they take the shape of a cow, then the essence of the cow is milk. And so Gita is that milk."

children.topic: One scripture, one God, one mantra, one work
children.note: Mahatmya verse 7: one scripture (Gita), one God (Krishna), one mantra (Hare Krishna) and one work (service to the Lord). — "Let there be one scripture only. One common scripture for the whole world."

children.topic: What aspect of my life needs clarity?
children.note: A reflection exercise: write down the one area of your life you want the Gita to clarify. — "If the Gita could clarify one aspect of my life today, what aspect would that be?"

children.topic: Qualification to access Gita: submissiveness
children.note: Although the Gita holds all answers, they open only to someone submissive to Krishna and willing to accept him as the Supreme. — "there is a qualification that is needed and that qualification is submissiveness. We have to be submissive to the Lord."

children.topic: Wikipedia needs an internet connection
children.note: All knowledge is online, but without a connection you cannot reach it; submissiveness is our connection to the Gita. — "in order to access that you need the internet connection isn't it without internet connection you cannot access Wikipedia so the same way"

children.topic: Front cover, middle, back cover
children.note: The 18 chapters divide into three sets of six: karma yoga (1-6), bhakti yoga (7-12) and jnana yoga (13-18); the essence is kept in the middle. — "front cover of Bhagat Gita is the first six chapters and that is known as karm yoga. The back cover is the last six chapters that is known as ghani yoga. But the middle is known as bakti yoga."

children.topic: Medicine bottles packed in the middle
children.note: We hide what is precious in the middle of the suitcase; Krishna put bhakti, the essence, in the middle six chapters. — "If you're carrying some glass bottles of medicine or whatever in your suitcase, you don't keep it on the edge, right? You keep it in between"

children.topic: Five topics of the Gita
children.note: The Gita deals with five subjects: prakriti (material nature), isvara (God), kala (time), karma (activities) and jiva (the soul). — "Priti means material nature. Ishwara. Ishwara means God. Kala Kala means time."

children.topic: Karma: activities or prescribed duties
children.note: The fourth topic, karma, covers our activities and duties. — "karma means activities or prescribed duties."

children.topic: Four yogas: linking with the Supreme
children.note: Wherever the word yoga appears it means connecting with the Supreme; the Gita covers four kinds and its essence is bhakti. — "Yoga means connection or linking to the supreme."

children.topic: Karma yoga: linking through action
children.note: When the linking process is mainly work or physical activity. — "requiring some action on our part then that is known as karma yoga."

children.topic: Jnana yoga: linking through knowledge
children.note: When the process is empirical, working things out with the mind. — "We're trying to figure things out with our mental capacities. Then that process is known as ghana yoga"

children.topic: Bhakti yoga: I am your servant
children.note: Engaging with the Lord in a devotional mood of service. — "you are the supreme lord I am your servant and that's why I'm engaging in your service then that is known as baki yoga"

children.topic: Essence of the Gita is bhakti yoga
children.note: Of the four, devotion is the heart of the Gita. — "the essence of Bhagat Gita is actually bakti yoga."

children.topic: Arjuna's crisis and surrender
Arjuna: draw my chariot between the armies
children.note: Arjuna knew exactly who he would fight; he asked to see them to gauge how determined they were. — "This is in text 22 of chapter 1. He said, "Oh infallible one, please draw my chariot between the two armies so that I may see those present here who desire to fight"

children.topic: Muhammad Ali versus question mark
children.note: No boxing match is advertised with an unknown opponent; Arjuna certainly knew his opponents. — "Muhammad Ali versus then a question mark. He'll know when he gets into the ring. Does that happen? No. So Arjuna didn't know who he was going to fight. He knew."

children.topic: The boxing stare down
children.note: Like boxers staring each other down at the weigh-in, Arjuna wanted to read his cousins' faces. — "So Arjuna wanted to see how determined are my cousins to fight with me. He wanted to see their face."

children.topic: Bhishma: a devotee on the wrong side
children.note: Bhishma, a pure devotee with an unbeaten record, fought for Duryodhana because Krishna wanted to show that even the greatest lose on the wrong side. — "Bishma Dave is a devotey of the Lord. He he is a devotey of Krishna. Lord Krishna is the charioteer of Arjuna on the other side and he's on this side."

children.topic: On the wrong side, you lose
children.note: However great a person is, being on the wrong side means game over. — "even if you're as good as Bishma as powerful as Bishma on the battlefield if you're on the wrong side you're going to lose."

children.topic: Last verse: where Krishna and Arjuna are, victory
children.note: Dhritarashtra's real question was 'who will win?'; Sanjaya answers it in the Gita's final verse. — "wherever Lord Krishna and Arjuna are that party will win."

children.topic: Arjuna's bodily symptoms on seeing family
children.note: Instead of warriors, Arjuna sees grandfather, uncle, cousin, teacher; he breaks down with about nine physical symptoms. — "So in text 28 to 30 Arjuna he is describing what he's going through when he saw the opposite party."

children.topic: Krishna points out family, not warriors
children.note: Krishna cleverly reframed the enemy as relatives, and Arjuna's attachment took over. — ""Oh see there is your grandfather, there is your uncle, there is your cousin, there is your friend, right? There's your teacher.""

children.topic: Trembling, dry mouth, hair standing on end
children.note: The list read out: limbs curling, dry mouth, trembling, hair on end, bow slipping, skin burning, unable to stand, forgetting himself, seeing only misfortune. — "My mouth is drying up. My whole body is trembling. My hair are standing on end."

children.topic: Exam hall panic
children.note: We all know Arjuna's breakdown: knowing the subject yet freezing when the exam paper is turned over. — "as soon as you flip the paper, you have a heart attack. You you you forget even what what the spelling of your own name is. Your pen is shaking."

children.topic: Karpanya dosha: miserly weakness
children.note: Arjuna admits he has all his strength, skill and strategy but cannot use any of it; this miserly weakness is what he brings to Krishna. — "my lord I have been afflicted by karpa karpa dsha means miserly weakness"

children.topic: Industrialist with torn socks
children.note: A wealthy company owner who came to the temple in torn socks: a true story of having but not using. — "That's a miser miser. You have the ability, you have the facilities, you have the requirements, but you don't use them."

children.topic: Plastic left on the remote
children.note: Gujaratis keeping the plastic wrap on a new remote: a lighter example of miserliness. — "they don't take out the plastic. No, it has to, you know, it has to remain perfect."

children.topic: Arjuna surrenders: I am your disciple
children.note: Not knowing what to do, Arjuna knew where to go; he surrendered to Krishna as a disciple and asked to be told what is best. — "I am your disciple shish and I am surrendered onto you I have come to you tell me what is best"

children.topic: We seek validation, not guidance
children.note: We want someone to say yes to our yes; Arjuna instead said 'I don't know, you tell me'. — "See nowadays when we go to people, we're looking for validation. We're not really looking for some advice or some guidance."

children.topic: Guru takes us from confusion to clarity
children.note: The Gita teaches that we need to approach a guru, someone in knowledge who can show the way. — "guru can take us out from confusion to clarity otherwise we remain in confusion"

children.topic: Take-home: when stuck, ask for help
children.note: The first lesson of the Gita and today's take-home: be intelligent enough to know you cannot figure it out alone. — "So when the problem is too big for us to solve, we should approach for help. Otherwise we get stuck."

children.topic: Krishna smiles, then blasts Arjuna
children.note: Once Arjuna finally asks what to do, Krishna smiles and then tells him his arguments make no sense. — "And so Lord Krishna he smiled a little bit at first right it wasn't a very big smile and it wasn't a laugh also."

children.topic: Wise lament neither for living nor dead
children.note: The verse on the board: Krishna says Arjuna speaks learned words but grieves for what is not worth grieving. — "Therefore he's saying the wise lament neither for the living nor for the dead."

children.topic: In crisis we forget who we are
children.note: Seeing relatives on the other side, Arjuna lost sight of his identity and his duty. — "he went into lamentation he forgot who he was he forgot what he was supposed to do he forgot his identity"

children.topic: Like a student who thinks exam is everything
children.note: A student in an exam feels it is the end of the world and forgets there is more to them than being a student. — "and we discussed just like the student at that moment when They're sitting the exam."

children.topic: Arjuna: my illusion is gone, I will act
children.note: After knowledge, duty and devotion, Arjuna surrenders and declares he will do as Krishna says. Krishna consciousness means acting according to Krishna's desire. — "my illusion is gone. My illusion is finished. I know who I am now. I know I am supposed to do what you say."

children.topic: Surrender means doing what Krishna says
children.note: Surrender is not sitting and doing nothing; Krishna's desire is already stated: think of Me, become My devotee, worship, bow down. — "No surrender means you do as Krishna is saying."

children.topic: Fighting because Krishna said fight
children.note: Arjuna is not fighting in the ordinary sense; he is doing Krishna consciousness, taking action with no personal want. — "Win, lose, doesn't matter. Krishna said fight so I'm fighting."

children.topic: Love gives milk, not Fanta
children.note: Love is not lip service or forgotten birthdays; a mother gives the child milk, not the Fanta she wants. Krishna has said clearly what pleases Him, so no speculation. — "So love means we do something for someone in the way that they want it to be done."

children.topic: Only Arjuna's consciousness changed
children.note: Arjuna did not run away or stop fighting; the same activity continued but for Krishna instead of for himself. — "He surrendered torishna. The surrender to Krishna changed what? Tell the devotey next to you. What do you think changed? Consciousness."

children.topic: Radio station WIFM: what's in it for me
children.note: Everyone is tuned to this station; Arjuna entered the battle asking what he would get and saw only dead relatives and sin. He then switched it off for what does Krishna want. — "It's called W I FM. Has anybody heard of it? W I FM? It's called What's in it for me?"

children.topic: Don't remove anything, just add Krishna
children.note: Arjuna came to fight and simply added Krishna; then there was victory, peace and happiness. — "Krishna consciousness or path of devotional service is not no no no no no. It's just add Krishna plus Krishna."

children.topic: The soul (jiva)
You are the soul, not the body
children.note: This is Krishna's first instruction in the Gita: remember your real identity. — "Lord Krishna immediately starts by reminding Arjuna who he is and he says you are the soul not the body."

children.topic: Krishna speaks of the soul only once
children.note: These key verses in Chapter 2 are the only place the Gita describes the soul; Arjuna understood in one shot. — "Lord Krishna speaks about the soul only once in the Gita. You will not find any information about the soul later on."

children.topic: Story: child crying 'my father's gone'
children.note: The father's body is lying right there, yet the child says he is gone; what has gone is the soul. — "there was a small child crying and [snorts] a sadhu was walking there and the sadhu asked him my dear child why are you crying"

children.topic: Living vs dead body: consciousness
children.note: The body itself is always dead matter; it moves only because the soul is present. — "so the difference between a living body and a dead body is consciousness. Actually the body is dead. See what moves the body is the soul."

children.topic: iPhone without a battery is useless
children.note: The phone is the body, the battery is the soul; however good the phone, without the battery it does nothing. — "can be the best iPhone but there's no battery inside it's useless isn't it? So the same way the body may be very strong, maybe very attractive but if there's no soul inside the body then it is useless."

children.topic: We say 'my hand', never 'I hand'
children.note: Our own language already admits that the body is a possession, separate from the self. — "We don't say I hand we don't say I ear right we say my hand my ear my body we don't say I body."

children.topic: Soul passes from boyhood to youth to old age
children.note: The body is a container; the same person passes through changing bodies and at death into another one. — "The soul passes from boyhood to youth to old age, right? I'm sure we all have family albums"

children.topic: Old photos: 'where did the hair go?'
children.note: Family albums show totally different bodies, yet everyone knows it is the same person. — "This was you. Where did the hair disappear? [laughter] And you're like, yeah, yeah, that was me."

children.topic: Soul cannot be destroyed, body cannot be saved
children.note: Two conclusions of the seers of truth; Arjuna wanted to save bodies that can never be saved. — "One soul can never be destroyed. And number two, the body can never be saved."

children.topic: If no one kills them, time will
children.note: No amount of gym or diet buys a guaranteed extension; every body must be destroyed by time. — "And even if someone else doesn't kill them, time will kill them. No matter how strong you are, how much gym hours you put in"

children.topic: Changing bodies like changing clothes
children.note: Old clothes are the old body; death is only a change of dress for the soul, which is never born and never dies. — "Just like we change old clothes and we put on new clothes, the soul similarly accepts new bodies after giving up old ones."

children.topic: No weapon can cut, burn, drown or dry the soul
children.note: Krishna speaks to the warrior in Arjuna's own language: no physical or elemental weapon can touch the soul. — "that the soul cannot be cut. That means no shastra can work acuh to the soul cannot be burnt cannot be drowned cannot be dried up by the wind."

children.topic: Astra (elemental) and shastra (physical) weapons
children.note: Arjuna knew both kinds of weapon, so the analogy of cutting, burning and drowning was tailored to him. — "So astra means it's elemental. Shastra means it's physical, right? Like swords and maces. These are shastras."

children.topic: The soul can never be killed. Full stop.
children.note: Krishna's last words on the soul in the Gita; no lamentation is needed for any living being. — "He says the soul can never be killed. Full stop. Right? And therefore you do not need to lament for any living being."

children.topic: Moving house: nobody laments the old one
children.note: Grandfathers and teachers leave old bodies for new ones, an upgrade; it is cause for happiness, not grief. — "So, they had a one-bedroom house, they'll get a two or a three, right? So, nobody laments, oh, why did you leave your old house?"

children.topic: Say it to your neighbour: body never alive, soul ever alive
children.note: The two-sentence conclusion each listener repeats to the devotee beside them. — "the bad news is body never alive. Body is dead. It's never alive. But the good news is soul is ever alive. Soul never dies."

children.topic: Six transformations of every body
children.note: Every body, human, animal or plant, goes through the same six changes; whatever is born must die. — "Birth, growth, stay for some time, produce byproducts, dwindle and then die. So everybody goes through this"

children.topic: A flower: bud, bloom, seed, wither
children.note: The flower shows all six transformations in miniature. — "Take a flower for example. It's in a bud form, then it blooms. Once it blooms, it stays for some time, then it starts producing a seed."

children.topic: After death, birth again: a cycle
children.note: Birth and death repeat; the cycle is no reason to lament or abandon duty. — "But then he's saying after death there's also birth. So this is a cycle and he's telling Arjuna you should not be disturbed by this cycle."

children.topic: If not the body, why do we suffer?
children.note: The answer drawn from the audience: because of the senses and because of attachment to the body. — "But then if we know this, why do we still suffer? If I go and slap someone, will they feel pain? But they're not the body."

children.topic: BMW hit on the highway: 'why did you hit me?'
children.note: The car stands for the body; nothing touched us, but attachment makes us feel every dent as pain. — "why did you hit me? Isn't it? Why did you hit me? He didn't hit you. He hit the car."

children.topic: Street kids vs your own kid
children.note: We ignore many street children but suffer for our own; the only difference is bodily relation and attachment. — "But if your kid ends up in the street, what happens? It's a lot of pain, isn't it?"

children.topic: Body is the field, soul the knower
children.note: Arjuna asks about kshetra and kshetrajna; Krishna answers that the body is a field of activities and the soul living inside it is the knower of that field. — "this body or son of counti is called the field and one who knows this body is called the knower of the field"

children.topic: Dehi: the one who lives in the body
children.note: The soul is the dweller, the body the dwelling; this distinction has run through all the earlier chapters. — "Dehi means one who lives in Deha. Deha is body. So the soul lives in the body."

children.topic: Farmer knows his own field
children.note: Just as a farmer knows his own farm but not others', the soul knows its own body: its pains and pleasures, not those of the person beside it. — "But you as a farmer you know right here I've planted carrots. Here I've planted peas. Here I've planted some beans."

children.topic: We are imperfect knowers even of ourselves
children.note: We know we are sick but not why; we do not know how food becomes blood or how many hairs are on our head. Our knowledge of our own field is partial. — "we ate the food we got food poisoning do we know what exactly caused the food poisoning we can't know"

children.topic: Eternal fragmental parts, struggling in the modes
children.note: The living entities are Krishna's eternal parts, but conditioned by the modes they struggle with the mind and senses. — "mango mame wango means you are my part you and I are connected we we are so connected with the lord even though we are here he is with us"

children.topic: The Gita is reverse engineering
children.note: Conditioning has engineered us into something we are not; the Gita is Krishna's mercy to undo it. This is not our natural place. — "Is reverse engineering. We have been engineered into something we are not. So but Lord Krishna is giving the knowledge by which we can reverse engineer come out right."

children.topic: Work (karma)
Everyone is forced to work (Chapter 3)
children.note: Arjuna asks why fight if bodies die anyway; Krishna answers that nobody can avoid work. — "Lord Krishna is saying to Arjuna, everyone has to work. Everyone is forced to work. There was uh I also do you know sessions"

children.topic: Nobody can sit still for two minutes
children.note: If we cannot stay idle for two minutes, giving up work altogether is impossible. — "just sit still for 2 minutes and I've even tried this with adults. 2 minutes people they they go crazy."

children.topic: Marshmallow experiment: mind on the object
children.note: Children who did not touch the marshmallow still thought of it constantly; not acting while dwelling on sense objects is pretending. — "And after like 4 minutes or so, most of them just ended up eating it."

children.topic: Stopping work artificially is pretension
children.note: Renouncing action before the heart is purified is a show; better to work. — "If you artificially stop your activities when that purification has not happened then it is called pretention."

children.topic: Yoga: duty without attachment to results
children.note: Arjuna's refusal to fight is itself an attachment; real yoga is doing prescribed work equipoised in success and failure. — "perform your duty equipoed abandoning All attachment to success and failure that is called yoga."

children.topic: Nobody sits an exam hoping to fail
children.note: Exams and interviews show how naturally we are attached to results; even Arjuna found this hard. — "Did anyone go and sit the exam and say it doesn't matter if I pass or fail?"

children.topic: Four results: no reaction, indifference to Vedas, no birth-death, samadhi
children.note: Working without expecting results brings freedom from reaction, from ritual, from rebirth, and leads to trance. — "Number two you become indifferent to the vedas. Whatever has been said, whatever has been written, it doesn't make a difference. Number three, there is no birth and no death."

children.topic: Musk and Buffett: working not for the money
children.note: The billionaire still going to work is a picture of acting where the result is not the motive. — "that someone like Jeff Bezos or Alon Musk they go to work it's not for the money whether the money is there or not there it's really makes no difference"

children.topic: Confectioner surrounded by sweets, no craving
children.note: Like the sweet-maker who does not eat sweets, one can be amid results without hankering for them; this is the higher consciousness of trance. — "They're surrounded by sweets the whole day that there is no drive to eat the sweets."

children.topic: Work done as sacrifice frees from bondage
children.note: The translation read aloud: work for Krishna's satisfaction and remain free; any other work binds. — "Work done as a sacrifice has to be performed. Otherwise, work causes bondage in this material world."

children.topic: Soldier gets a medal, neighbour-killer gets jail
children.note: The same act on behalf of authority earns a medal; done for oneself it earns prison. Acting for Krishna is the medal. — "So if a soldier kills an enemy soldier, what do the government give him? Medal, right?"

children.topic: Practice tonight: offer your food to Krishna
children.note: We are neither vegetarians nor non-vegetarians but prasad eaters; offered food carries no karma. — "But Lord Krishna is saying if you do that as a sacrifice to me then there is no reaction. So if we offer our food to Krishna then there is no reaction."

children.topic: Patram pushpam: leaf, flower, fruit, water
children.note: Krishna specifies what may be offered; whatever is offered, he takes away the karma. That is yajna. — "he gives a list patam pushpam toyam four things flowers, fruits, water and leaves you just this."

children.topic: Using Krishna's facilities for ourselves is stealing
children.note: Like printing party posters on the office printer: earth, water, light and air are Krishna's resources. — "the light, he's given us the air, but instead of using it in his service, we are using it in our service. And therefore, we are stealing."

children.topic: Lotus leaf untouched by water
children.note: One who does duty without attachment and surrenders results to the Lord is untouched by sin, as water glides off a waxy lotus leaf. — "he is not touched by sin just like a lotus leaf is not touched by water"

children.topic: Do not detach from work; be detached in work
children.note: Good or bad results both keep us stuck here, so the aim is no result at all: work without attachment. — "work. Don't run away from work but become detached in work."

children.topic: Mother serves the child expecting nothing
children.note: Prabhupada's closest example of detached service: the mother continues serving whether or not the child ever repays her. — "When the mother has the child, does the mother serve the child because she gets something from the child?"

children.topic: Intention matters more than the work
children.note: The verse on sacrifice in knowledge is read; work done with the intention of offering it to Krishna outweighs the work or its result. — "Intention behind the work is more important than the work itself."

children.topic: Doctor's knife vs attacker's knife
children.note: Same act, different intention: we pay the doctor to cut us because he intends to heal. — "The doctor has a knife and another person has a knife."

children.topic: Hardworking child vs PS5 child both fail
children.note: The same failed result is treated differently by parents depending on effort and intention. — "Let's say you have another child and they're on their PS5 the whole night and they're not even interested in studying."

children.topic: Material consciousness gives material result
children.note: Studying to buy a house in Sandton yields only a material result; the same work in spiritual consciousness leads out. — "So if we perform a material activity with material consciousness we'll get a material result."

children.topic: We work only to enjoy the results
children.note: Sacrifice means controlling the senses: Krishna tells Arjuna to work and forget the result, which is the opposite of how we normally live. — "To achieve results. And what are you going to do with those results? Enjoy them, right? Yeah. That's the only reason why we do anything."

children.topic: Survey: hate the boss, love the salary
children.note: People endure a job they hate purely for the result at the end; this shows how attached we are to results. — "we hate the boss, we hate the colleagues, and we also hate the work."

children.topic: Visa for sanatana dhama
children.note: If an American visa is hard, entry to the eternal abode is earned through the work of sacrifice. — "imagine a visa for sanatan dham. You're not going to just go to a shop and buy the visa. You have to work for it."

children.topic: Live to eat vs eat to live
children.note: A traveller touring the world for cuisine stands for living for sense pleasure; the Gita reverses it - do something to get nothing. — "They live to eat. But Gita is telling us eat to live. Opposite."

children.topic: Quiz: karma, vikarma or akarma?
children.note: Six everyday scenarios that the audience sorts into the three kinds of action. — "If you want to remember karma karma means good result. V karma means bad result. And akarma means no result."

children.topic: Student studying for marks and career: karma
children.note: No one is harmed, but a result is wanted, so it is karma. — "a student studies hard because she wants admiration, high marks, and a better paying career."

children.topic: Falsified expense claim: vikarma
children.note: Dishonest gain, even unnoticed, is forbidden action with a bad reaction. — "here so that's V karma you falsify explains claims the many salesmen usually do this and they get a perdm"

children.topic: Food offered to Krishna then served: akarma
children.note: Cooking with devotion and offering first produces no reaction. — "that's clearly a karma Yeah. No reaction. It's offered to Krishna and then it's fed to the family."

children.topic: Attain perfection by worshipping through work
children.note: Chapter 18 text 46: do the karma the Vedas give you, not sin, and it becomes worship that takes you out. — "by worship of the Lord who is the source of all beings and who is all pervading a man can attain perfection through performing his own work."

children.topic: Running away is not the answer
children.note: Arjuna wanted to give up fighting and beg; Krishna insists on doing one's work and worshipping Him through it. — "I want to go to the Himalayas and beg. Lord Krishna said no you can't run away. Lord Krishna said no running away is not the answer."

children.topic: Three Rs turn work into worship
children.note: The acharyas' formula: righteous work, reward offered to Krishna, and remembrance of Krishna while working. — "this formula is called three R three R. So if we do these three Rs then our work will become worship. The first R is righteous."

children.topic: Righteous work uplifts society
children.note: Righteous is not just honest; it must actually help others rather than damage society, so inflating a government tender fails the test. — "So righteous work means work that helps others, not help myself or not help my people, but work that actually uplifts society"

children.topic: Factory of 3,000 workers making liquor
children.note: Supporting 3,000 families sounds righteous until you learn the product is liquor; the harm to society decides the answer. — "That factory is a liquor factory. So, [laughter] so now is it righteous work or no?"

children.topic: Reward: offer the fruit to Krishna
children.note: The second R: whatever the work earns is given to Krishna, partly or wholly. — "We worked but the reward is yours my lord. Either in part or in full. So that's the second way."

children.topic: Remembrance: fight but remember Me
children.note: The third R: remember who the work is for. Usually one of the Rs is missing, most often remembrance. — "Lord Krishna tells Arjuna you fight on the battlefield but remember me."

children.topic: Why bad things happen to good people
children.note: Suffering in this body comes from what was done in previous bodies, and the Supersoul saw all of it. — "So this answers the question why do bad things happen to good people. I am I I've not hurt anybody. I've not stolen from anyone."

children.topic: Who saw? The rasgullas story
children.note: We think a wrong nobody saw does not count, but Krishna says: I saw, and I permitted it because you wanted it. — "There were too few rasgulas here in the temple hall. Nobody was there. I ate them. You can't accuse me of eating because nobody saw, right?"

children.topic: Sun, moon, demigods and Chitragupta also see
children.note: Answer to a question about Chitragupta: even if one hides from all the elements and demigods, the Lord in the heart is always there. — "The sun sees, the moon sees, other demigods see like the air etc. And then Chitra Gupta, as you rightly said, he also sees."

children.topic: The Lord (isvara)
Why the speaker is called Sri Bhagavan
children.note: Dhritarashtra, Arjuna and Sanjaya are named as speakers, but Krishna's words are marked 'Sri Bhagavan uvaca'. — "There were four speakers in Gita. There's one more speaker. Apart from Arjuna darashtra and Krishna there's one more speaker. Sanjaya."

children.topic: Bhagavan possesses six opulences
children.note: Bhagavan means the one who has all strength, knowledge, beauty, fame, renunciation and wealth in full. — "One who possesses all opulences which are usually classified into six. Uh one who has all strength, all knowledge, all beauty, fame, renunciation and which is the last one? Wealth."

children.topic: Krishna chooses his birth; we do not
children.note: The verse on Krishna's appearance is read from the screen. Unlike us, the Lord is not forced to take birth; he appears by his own will. — "I chose the day. I chose the place. I chose the parents. I even chose the time. That is what differentiates us from him."

children.topic: We chose no parents, place, day, time
children.note: Nobody in the audience chose where or to whom they were born; we come because we are forced to. — "No time, no day, no place, no parents. But Lord Krishna, he's saying I am not like you."

children.topic: Ishvara: the Lord controls his own coming
children.note: This introduces the third of the five topics, the controller. We call ourselves controllers but control nothing about our birth. — "Now we're looking at the topic of ishwara controller. Lord controls his time to come."

children.topic: Three reasons Krishna comes
children.note: To protect his devotees, to destroy those who disturb them, and to establish the principles of religion. — "Number one to deliver the pious. Number two to annihilate the miscreants. So one is to protect his devotees."

children.topic: Do not disturb Krishna's devotees
children.note: We want to be in the first category, protected as devotees, not in the second. — "We should not disturb Krishna's devotees because if we disturb Krishna's devotees, then he comes looking for us, right?"

children.topic: Absolute Truth is God plus His energies
children.note: Devotees say Absolute Truth rather than God because Krishna is described together with His energies. — "And the absolute truth is God plus. There is a plus. And so this is Lord Krishna is telling us about the plus."

children.topic: GOD: generator, operator, destroyer
children.note: The ordinary meaning of God; the Absolute Truth adds His energies to this. — "God means generator, operator, destroyer. G O D, right? God, generator, operator, destroyer."

children.topic: Sun with its heat and light
children.note: A sun without heat or light is no sun; the Lord is the energetic and His energies are inseparable from Him. — "So, sun plus its energies. Sun with the heat and light. Similarly, the lord has is the energetic. He is the supreme and he has energies."

children.topic: Two energies: material and spiritual
children.note: Krishna describes an inferior material energy and a superior energy, the living entities, who come from Him. — "Material energy means it is made of matter or elements. Earth, water, air, fire, ether. These are the gross elements. Right? And then there is a spiritual nature. And that is us."

children.topic: No truth superior to Krishna
children.note: Since spirit and matter are both His energy and nothing exists outside them, Krishna is the source of everything. — "So therefore Lord Krishna is saying everything is my energy. And further on he says there is nothing superior to me."

children.topic: Moses asked 'Who are you?'
children.note: Other scriptures lack the emphatic declaration Krishna makes about Himself in the Gita. — "I am who I am. Right? But in the Gita he's saying clearly [snorts] there is no truth above me. I am the supreme."

children.topic: Chapter 10: see Krishna in everything
children.note: Chapter 10, Vibhuti-yoga, teaches how to remember Krishna by seeing Him in the things around us. — "how we can see Krishna in everything is chapter 10 Lord Krishna he tells Arjuna how Arjuna can see some things around the world and remember him"

children.topic: The Gita in four verses
children.note: Four verses of chapter 10 are widely accepted as the essence of the whole Gita, repeating what Krishna has been saying in earlier chapters. — "Lord Krishna gives us the entire Bhagat Gita in four shlokas. This is known as the Chhatur shloki Bhagat Gita."

children.topic: I am the source of everything
children.note: We are souls who came from Krishna; everything we have came from Krishna; so our relationship is to engage in His service. — "I am the source of all spiritual and material worlds. Everything emanates from me. The wise who perfectly know this engage in my devote"

children.topic: A finger is useless off the hand
children.note: The finger stands for the soul and the body for Krishna: attached and obedient, the finger is complete and happy; detached, it is thrown away. — "If I want to pick up something with my finger, the finger has to obey my order. It can't say no."

children.topic: Pure devotees' thoughts dwell in me
children.note: Text 9: devotees do not serve begrudgingly; they get bliss from serving and from talking about Krishna with one another. — "The thoughts of my pure devotees dwell in me. Their lives are fully devoted to my service and they derive great"

children.topic: Fish cannot live without water
children.note: For a devotee, life without Krishna is no life at all, just as a fish must be in water to be happy. — "for devotees living without Krishna is like a fish living without water. Fish cannot live without water."

children.topic: Chapter 11: everything is in Krishna
children.note: Arjuna asks Krishna to prove He is the Supreme Lord, so Krishna shows the universal form. Chapter 10 was Krishna in everything; chapter 11 is everything in Krishna. — "Krishna is telling Arjuna how he can remember him by seeing everything within this world. So then next Arjuna asks okay but how do I know you are Krishna?"

children.topic: Time I am, destroyer of the worlds
children.note: Krishna declares Himself as time, come to destroy everyone on the battlefield except the Pandavas. — "worlds and I have come here to destroy all people with the exception of you the pandas. All the soldiers here on both sides will be slain."

children.topic: Thousands of heads, arms and legs
children.note: In the universal form Arjuna saw all planets and demigods, and even himself, within Krishna. — "Hundreds and thousands of heads, hundreds and thousands of arms, hundreds and thousands of legs. Right? In other words, Lord Krishna showed him how everything is in him."

children.topic: Soldiers rushing into the mouth
children.note: Arjuna saw the Kaurava and Pandava soldiers being devoured, became frightened, and asked who this form was. — "they were all rushing into the mouth of this form and they were being chewed. And so Arjuna got scared and he asked Lord Krishna who are you?"

children.topic: Krishna is the source of all forms
children.note: Universal form, form of time, four-handed Vishnu form and finally the original two-armed form: chapter 11 settles that Vishnu comes from Krishna, not the reverse. — "So he is the source of all forms. The forehanded, the universal, the kala rupa, everything comes from Lord Krishna. That's what he's showing in chapter 11."

children.topic: The Lord is the second knower of all bodies
children.note: Besides the soul, who knows one body partially, there is a second knower, the Supreme Lord, who knows every body completely. — "there is a second knower and that is the Lord. He knows all bodies. He knows what's happening in each and every single body."

children.topic: Lands department knows every farm
children.note: The individual farmer knows only his own land; the lands department knows every parcel in the country. So the Lord knows all bodies while we know only ours. — "But the government official one who's working in the lands department he knows all farms all lands isn't it?"

children.topic: Supersoul is the overseer and permitter
children.note: Krishna defines Himself in the body as the proprietor with two functions: to oversee and to permit. — "yet in this body there's another a transcendental enjoyer who is the lord the supreme proprietor who exists as the overseer and perimeter And who is known as the super soul."

children.topic: Two functions: oversee and permit
children.note: Out of love the Lord accompanies the soul into every body, watching everything it does and sanctioning what it wants. — "To oversee and to permit. Right? You see there are two words there overseer and permeter. So to oversee and to permit."

children.topic: Seated in the heart: remembrance and forgetfulness
children.note: Krishna in the heart supplies whichever we ask for: if we wish to forget Him He helps us forget, if we wish to remember Him He helps us remember. — "I'm seated in everyone's heart and from me comes remembrance, knowledge and forgetfulness. By all the veas I am to be known indeed I am the compiler of vanta"

children.topic: Personal doctor always on call
children.note: The Supersoul is constantly on call; we only need to dial. — "It's like having your own personal doctor, you know, on call. Anything just call and he's there, right?"

children.topic: Hare Krishna is His speed dial number
children.note: Chant Hare Krishna and He is there before the mantra is even finished. — "This is his speed dial number. Just in case anyone wants to have, you know, speed dial, you put on speed dial on your phones and you want his number."

children.topic: He picks up, but we stop responding
children.note: Answer to whether Krishna also calls us: He is not limited and answers whoever calls His name; the problem is that we then do not talk to Him. — "We immediately call him, he picks up immediately and then we like oh no, now we don't want to talk to you."

children.topic: Madhva's two fingers: soul and Supersoul
children.note: Madhvacharya preached vigorously against the earlier school that taught we are God; he held up two fingers to show there are always two knowers, soul and Supersoul. — "We're two separate knowers. We have an acharia. His name was Madva."

children.topic: Two fingers means two separate knowers
children.note: Remember the two fingers: nobody should convince you after today that you are God. — "But Madvachaya used to hold up two fingers like this. Two fingers meaning two"

children.topic: Man and Superman
children.note: Supersoul means He can do what the soul cannot: He knows all bodies, not just one. — "just like we have man and then we have superman. Isn't it? So superman does things that man cannot do."

children.topic: Nature and the three modes (prakriti)
Contact with nature conditions the soul
children.note: Because of desires we associate with the three modes of material nature, and this contact changes our original nature. — "Goodness, passion and ignorance. When the internality [cough] comes into contact with nature becomes conditioned by these becomes conditioned."

children.topic: Air conditioner changes the air
children.note: Conditioned means altered: as hot air is made cool by an air conditioner, the soul's original nature is changed by the modes. — "coming hot, it goes through an air conditioner and it becomes conditioned to become cool."

children.topic: Guna literally means rope
children.note: The modes tie the soul, and the effect depends on how much one associates with each. — "these are known as the goonas the three goonas and gona literally means rope literally you're tied"

children.topic: Modes are the bars of the prison
children.note: We cannot leave the body at will, nor fly or eat grass in it: bound by the body and the body bound by the world. — "These are like the bars in the prison. See material nature and the world here we are bound. We are bound to our bodies."

children.topic: Conditions: shoes off, seat belt, no opening the door
children.note: Entering the temple or boarding a plane carries conditions; this world's condition is that you stay until you develop the desire to return to Krishna. — "you want to come into the temple hall there's one condition what is the condition to come into the temple hall very first condition take your shoes off"

children.topic: Goodness illuminates, passion binds, ignorance deludes
children.note: Three verses read aloud: goodness conditions by happiness and knowledge, passion by longing and fruitive action, ignorance by madness, indolence and sleep. — "the goodness pure love is illuminating and frees one from all sinful reactions. Those situations in that mode become conditioned by sense of happiness and knowledge."

children.topic: Passion: unlimited desires and longing
children.note: Passion binds the soul to fruitive work through endless desire. — "The motor passion is born of unlimited size and longing both son and because of this the living entity is bound to material through actions."

children.topic: Three modes as three primary colours
children.note: Goodness is yellow, passion is red and ignorance is blue. Just as three primary colours mix into every other colour, the three modes mix into every kind of body. — "So if you were to assign these three primary colors to the modes of material nature, what color would you give?"

children.topic: Red is energetic passion, yellow calm goodness
children.note: Passion is intense activity and endless desires, so it gets red; goodness is calm and composed, so it gets yellow; ignorance gets blue. — "And yellow means calm, composed, uh cool, right? That's goodness."

children.topic: Mixed modes produce millions of bodies
children.note: Every body is a particular combination of the three modes, which is why there are so many species. — "if you combine the three modes you get combinations and according to these combinations you get bodies and according to the bodies there are millions of them."

children.topic: Morning goodness, noon passion, night ignorance
children.note: Pair exercise mapping the modes onto the day: fresh and calm in the morning, wide awake and wanting at noon, tired and lazy at night. — "Mode of goodness in the morning. Goodness in the mornings. The mode of passion at noon. The mode of passion at noon. And the mode of darkness at night."

children.topic: When the sun is down, inauspicious things happen
children.note: Even for night-shift workers, night generally belongs to ignorance; nobody steals in broad daylight (outside South Africa, he jokes). — "See the sun is down. So when the sun is down all sorts of inospicious activities happen."

children.topic: Modes are always in motion, always fighting
children.note: Not a fixed rule: someone can be sleepy in the morning. One mode takes over the other two, yet a person can be mainly situated in one. — "these modes are always in motion. It is not fixed. Right. They're always in motion. Sometimes there's goodness, sometimes passion, sometimes ignorance."

children.topic: Foods in the three modes
children.note: The verses on food read aloud: juicy, wholesome foods are goodness; bitter, spicy, burning foods are passion; stale, decomposed, putrid and untouchable foods are ignorance. — "Foods dear to those in the mode of goodness increase the duration of life, purify one's existence and give strength, health, happiness and satisfaction."

children.topic: Ignorance: stale, decomposed, untouchable
children.note: Food in ignorance. — "Food prepared more than 3 hours before being eaten. Food that is tasteless, decomposed and putrid. And food consisting of remnants and untouchable things is dear to those in the mode of darkness."

children.topic: Mushrooms, onion, garlic are untouchable
children.note: Attraction to these foods indicates the mode of ignorance. — "things like mushrooms, untouchable. This is fungi, right? Onion, garlic, all these things are untouchable things."

children.topic: Happiness in the modes: poison and nectar
children.note: Happiness in goodness is poison first and nectar later; in passion nectar first and poison later; in ignorance delusion from beginning to end. — "That's in which the beginning may be just like poison but at the end is just like nectar in which awakenings want to selfreization is said to be happiness in order of goodness."

children.topic: Student, exams and the World Cup
children.note: In goodness he studies through the torture and passing is nectar; in passion he watches the matches and failing is poison; in ignorance he does not bother at all. — "World Cup is going on. You can't watch the match. You have to study for your exam. Oh, why? This is torture."

children.topic: Three gates to hell: lust, anger, greed
children.note: Text 21 of the chapter on divine and demoniac natures: these three are the first-class tickets to hell, so avoid them and the modes that produce them. — "Lust, anger, and greed. Every sane man should give these up for they lead to the degradation of the soul."

children.topic: Anger is the younger brother of lust
children.note: When desire is frustrated we become angry; kamanuja means the one born after lust. — "So anger is the younger brother of lust. Another name for anger is kamanuja."

children.topic: One more rasgula: greed the elder brother
children.note: When desire is fulfilled we want more; that is greed, the elder brother who always follows lust. — "Oh, that rasgula was very nice, very tasty. Can I have one more?"

children.topic: Get it: greed. Don't get it: anger
children.note: Lust comes first; both possible outcomes of a desire lead to another of the three gates. — "If we get what we want we become greedy. If we don't get what we want we become angry."

children.topic: Modes are invisible bars of a jail
children.note: The modes are also the strings that tie us; reaching goodness leaves only one string to break. — "we say this is like the modes are like the bars of the jail cell. We can't see them, but they keep us here."

children.topic: Easier to break one rope than three
children.note: Coming to goodness reduces the bondage to one string, which is easier to break. — "it's easier to break one string than to break three, isn't it? If you have three ropes tying you very tightly, it's very hard to get out."

children.topic: Go to Krishna, who has no strings
children.note: The easiest way out is to approach the one who is not bound by the modes at all. — "the easiest way is actually to go to a person who has no strings and that is Krishna Krishna says I can open them for you"

children.topic: Goodness is the ladder to climb out
children.note: Come at least to goodness; from there management is easier and Krishna consciousness becomes possible, even though goodness itself is eventually left behind. — "It's like a ladder. You use goodness to climb and once you reach the top then you don't leave the ladder anymore."

children.topic: Devotee fell asleep eating prasad
children.note: In ignorance you are sleepy all the time and cannot read the Gita or chant; even eating prasad becomes impossible. — "I have even seen a devotey who was so tired they fell asleep while eating prasan."

children.topic: Engineer your day to promote goodness
children.note: Divine qualities follow naturally when the day is redesigned around goodness. — "we have to engineer our lifestyle. We have to reinvent our day in such a way that we are promoting goodness more than the other two."

children.topic: Calm versus hooting in a traffic jam
children.note: Behaviour in a traffic jam shows the difference between a person in goodness and one agitated by passion. — "there people who are calm who are collected they're listening to some lecture or they're listening to some kan behind the steering wheel and others are horning and honking and cursing"

children.topic: Only bhakti transcends the modes
children.note: One who engages in unfailing devotional service at once transcends the modes; there is no other escape. — "Lord Krishna is saying only through bacti only through devotional service can you transcend the modes of nature"

children.topic: Iron rod in fire becomes fire
children.note: By constant association with Krishna, who is above the modes, the devotee takes on Krishna's qualities, as an iron rod in fire becomes red hot and burns like fire. — "You take an iron rod and you put it in fire. Over time, what happens to the iron rod?"

children.topic: Bhakti is the hack, the shortcut out
children.note: Any activity of devotional service, like the temple itself, is not under the modes because it is connected to Krishna. — "bacti is like the hack it's like the means out the shortcut to come out"

children.topic: Prabhupada in the Bowery
children.note: A devotee connected to Krishna is not affected by degraded surroundings; likewise devotees chanting on Ratha-yatra did not even notice the market they passed. — "shap praad had to jump over people to enter his room they were lying there on the floor like completely out of it right but he would stay there because he's connected to Krishna."

children.topic: Desires decide which body we get
children.note: The Lord sees and records every desire and supplies a body suited to fulfil it, in sequence. — "according to our desire and according to the magnitude of our desires Lord Krishna fulfills them by giving us various bodies in which we can carry out those desires."

children.topic: Man who wants to live in water becomes a fish
children.note: Prabhupada's example: someone who spends all day at the Durban beach gets a fish body next life so the desire can be fulfilled naturally. — "why you artificially trying to be a fish next life we'll give you a body of a fish you can stay in the water full time why do it artificially"

children.topic: Meat-eater and tiger, sleeper and bear
children.note: Old Gita editions picture a meat-eater beside a tiger and a heavy sleeper beside a bear: nature gives the body that matches the desire. — "Nature will give a body where you don't have to cook anything. You just go and you have nails and you have teeth and you can just rip open the animal and eat the flesh."

children.topic: Karma is like cash
children.note: Karma dictates where we take birth and what body we get; like cash, it limits which desires can actually be bought. — "you have cash, you want to buy a house. According to the amount of cash you have, you can buy a house."

children.topic: Time (kala)
Kala-rupa: the form of time
children.note: What Arjuna saw was Krishna as time. Whether Arjuna fought or not, the soldiers were already finished; only the Pandavas had return tickets. — "Krishna showed was the kala rupa the form of time. I've already killed all these people. When they came into Kuruketra they came with a one-way ticket."

children.topic: I did the work, you take the credit
children.note: Krishna has already done everything; Arjuna is invited simply to act and receive the credit. — "I have already killed all these people. They're all dead. You cannot help them. But I want you to take the credit."

children.topic: Only devotees outlast time
children.note: Alexander, the Roman and British empires are all gone, but Arjuna and Hanuman are still spoken of; devotees conquer time. — "Pandovas 5,000 years ago, still going on. That is only 5,000. What about Lord Hanuman? traa 1 million years ago still talking about him."

children.topic: This form is not for devotees
children.note: Kala-rupa destroys everyone who is not a devotee; devotees have nothing to fear from it. — "He said except the pandavas this form is not for you. It's not for the devotees. This form is for those who are not devotees."

children.topic: The cat, the kitten and the rat
children.note: Prabhupada's example: the same mouth of time that means death for the rat carries the kitten to safety. The devotee is the kitten. — "So, kala rupa if we equate it to the cat and then the devotey is the kitten. When the cat catches the kitten, the kitten is safe."

children.topic: For the rat it is a one-way ticket
children.note: The soldiers being eaten were the rat in the cat's mouth; the Pandavas were the kittens. — "But the same cat catches a rat, the rat knows now this was a one-way ticket. Yeah. So the same way Kala Rupa"

children.topic: Moths into fire, rivers into ocean
children.note: Arjuna saw the envious (Duryodhana, Karna) rushing in like moths into fire, while the favourable (Bhishma, Drona) merged like rivers into the ocean. — "those who are enimical to Krishna but those who are favorable to Krishna he says I see them as rivers go into an ocean"

children.topic: Dhruva stood on the head of death
children.note: Dhruva Maharaja's fearlessness shows how devotees relate to time; yet, like Arjuna, they do not wish to see this form and ask for the two-armed form. — "Duva Maharaj. When death came, he stood on the head of death. He told death no problem I am not afraid of you."

children.topic: Remember Krishna at death, go to Krishna
children.note: Chapter 8: one who leaves the body remembering Krishna attains His nature without doubt. — "if you remember Lord Krishna at the time of death you go to Krishna At the time of death, he comes to my nature. My nature means my abboard."

children.topic: Personal assistant flies with the boss
children.note: A good assistant travels and stays with the boss; a devotee stays with Krishna in His abode. — "If the personal assistant is serving nicely, they say, oh, no, no, you know, two seats."

children.topic: Whatever you think at death, you attain
children.note: Two points: a controlled mind lets us think of Krishna at death, and our final thought decides our next state. — "Whatever thoughts you have at the time of death that state you will attain"

children.topic: Can I just remember Krishna at death?
children.note: The lecturer dismantles the idea of enjoying freely now and remembering Krishna only at the end. — "I'll remember Krishna at the time of death up till that point I can do what I want. Is there a problem with that?"

children.topic: No expiry label on our heads
children.note: Death can come anytime, as the Nepal floods showed; even a Baba's astrology date does not help. — "Does anyone know when they're going to expire? Did we come with the expiry label on our heads? Best before? No."

children.topic: Parrot said 'caw' not 'Ram'
children.note: When the cat caught it, the parrot's real attachment came out; whatever we put in is what comes out at death. — "The parrot wasn't saying ram ram ram. [laughter] Yeah. Parrot was saying cow cow cow."

children.topic: Spot exam: ready because you studied daily
children.note: If we always think of Krishna, the time of death does not matter. — "Today is your spot exam, you know." Okay, I'm ready. I studied."

children.topic: No shortcut within the shortcut
children.note: Chanting is already the shortcut; we still have to put in the work and make thinking of Krishna our default. — "in kalyuga everyone is looking for a shortcut cut in the shortcut. So we already have a shortcut but we like no can can we can we can we get a shorter thing"

children.topic: He descends when religion declines
children.note: The verse read from the screen gives the timing of the Lord's appearance: when irreligion rises and religion declines. — "Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice or descendants of a prominent prominent rise of religion at that time I desend myself."

children.topic: Become an instrument (nimitta-matram)
children.note: Krishna tells Arjuna to fight and win glory because the outcome is already decided; Arjuna's role is only to be the instrument. — "So Lord Krishna said, "I've already dealt with everything. I've already sorted everything. You just need to be an instrument."

children.topic: Pandavas argue who was the greatest warrior
children.note: After the war Bhima, Arjuna and the brothers debated who won the battle; Krishna declined to judge and sent them to a witness. — "Bhima was saying I killed 100 sons of the koravas of of the of duryodhan the koravas I killed 100 I am the greatest warrior"

children.topic: Barbarika saw only Krishna killing
children.note: Bhima's son Barbarika, who watched the whole battle as a head without a body, saw only Krishna doing everything. — "he said no I could only see Krishna all over the battlefield fil killing everyone. Yeah. Then the pandas understood, oh our name is coming but the work wasn't ours."

children.topic: Central message: surrender and be used
children.note: Pure devotees know they are doing nothing; Prabhupada always said his guru had sent everyone to help him. When devotees think 'I am doing', Krishna sends reminders. — "that's why he's saying nima matram become an instrument and this is the again the central message of Krishna and Gita is that become an instrument surrender"

children.topic: Krishna serves the devotee harder
children.note: The relationship is reciprocal and sweet; it cannot be understood without engaging in devotional service oneself. — "the harder the devotees try to serve Krishna the harder Krishna serves the devotees we take one step he takes 10 steps that is the sweet relationship"

children.topic: The mind
Mind can be friend or enemy
children.note: Krishna's teaching in chapter 6 that the mind is the friend of one who has conquered it and the enemy of one who has not. — "Mind can be the friend and can also be the enemy. Now, how does it become the friend or how does it become the enemy?"

children.topic: Controlled mind is a friend
children.note: The difference is simply who is in charge: you or the mind. — "So if we are able to control the mind then it becomes our friend. If we become controlled by the mind then it is our enemy."

children.topic: No link with the Lord without mind control
children.note: Martial arts, studies or any spiritual path all require a controlled mind. — "We cannot link up with the supreme without mind control. Any path you take, any discipline you take,"

children.topic: Are you using the phone or is it using you?
children.note: An audience exercise that sets up the mind as a tool that can either serve us or hijack us. — "Are you using the phone or is the phone using you? Okay. Quickly to the devotey sitting next to you."

children.topic: Phone hijacks time like the mind
children.note: A five-minute break becomes hours down a rabbit hole; the mind does the same thing to us. — "The phone somehow hijacks the time, isn't it? So, you have a schedule."

children.topic: Mind is a tool, like a knife
children.note: A knife or phone is good or bad depending on use; so is the mind. — "the phone is a tool. Just like here Lord Krishna will say the mind is a tool. Now if we utilize the tool properly then we are good."

children.topic: Give the mind a ring to stay in
children.note: Boxers stay in the ring; the mind needs a boundary too. That boundary is regulation. — "So that's the frame that the speaker has to be in. Cannot leave. So we need to give the mind also a ring or a circle to stay in."

children.topic: TEDx red circle
children.note: The speaker's frame on stage stands for the limits regulation gives to the mind. — "The speaker or the presenter cannot go out of that red circle. Has to be in that red circle."

children.topic: Bull tied to a pole
children.note: The rope stands for regulation that keeps the mind from running away. — "the bull can move around as much as the rope allows, but not more than that. So we have to give the mind a ring, a circle or a rope to keep it centered"

children.topic: Arjuna: mind harder to control than wind
children.note: Hearing the full dhyana yoga process, Arjuna protests that the flickering mind is impossible to control, and Krishna agrees it is difficult. — "It may be possible to control the wind but I find to control the mind is impossible. And so Lord Krishna said yes what you have said is correct."

children.topic: Practice and detachment control the mind
children.note: Krishna's answer to Arjuna: abhyasa (regular practice) and vairagya (detachment). — "abiasa and vayaya these are the two tools that Lord Krishna mentions to control the mind by suitable practice that is abasa and detachment means Vaya"

children.topic: Chanting the maha mantra is our practice
children.note: For devotees, abhyasa means regular chanting of Hare Krishna. — "What practice do we employ to help us control the mind? Chanting of the mahantra. Chanting of the maha mantra."

children.topic: Mantra frees the mind by constraining it
children.note: Man means mind, tra means to free; the holy names anchor the mind and give it a place to rest. — "Ironically freeing the mind means constraining it. Right? We are we usually have the opposite uh idea that to free the mind means there should be no restraints"

children.topic: Rules of detachment in our lifestyle
children.note: Vairagya for devotees means the regulative principles: no tea, coffee, liquor, meat, eggs or fish. — "There are some rules and regulations we give to ourselves in our lifestyle that help control the mind. Right. And these are very scientific."

children.topic: British lord who wanted to be a brahmana
children.note: People find the principles hard only because they lack the right frame; with it they are not hard at all. — "can make you a brahmana no follow these four rules. And then the Lord said impossible."

children.topic: Regulate eating, sleeping, work, recreation
children.note: Krishna's method for controlling the mind begins with a regulated lifestyle. — "So one who is regulated in his eating vihara means to sleep. One who is regulated in his sleep. One who regulated in his work and recreation. Such a person can attain peace."

children.topic: Breakfast in traffic, lunch at the desk
children.note: Modern life with no fixed time or diet for eating makes the mind impossible to control. — "they're having breakfast in traffic because they got late. Yeah. Either they have some coffee and some buns or something"

children.topic: Catching up sleep on the weekend
children.note: Irregular sleep, early, late or none at all, keeps the mind unsteady. — "So I spent the weekend catching up my sleep, right? It doesn't work that way by the way."

children.topic: Lust pushes us to sin
children.note: Arjuna asks why people do what they should not; Krishna names lust as the driver. — "Arjuna is saying why do people do v karma? Why do they want to perform sin? What makes them perform sin? And Lord Krishna says it is lust."

children.topic: All-devouring sinful enemy of the world
children.note: Controlled by intelligence and knowledge, lust stops vikarma and karma so only akarma remains. — "See lust is very very it's the all devouring sinful enemy of the world. It pushes us to commit sin."

children.topic: Rasgulla vanishes: 'I don't know'
children.note: Nobody teaches a child to lie; sin comes naturally because lust is already within. — "you just leave a rasgula on the table and the child is roaming around and after some minutes the rasgula has disappeared."

children.topic: Control senses by knowledge, steady the mind
children.note: The closing point; where that spiritual intelligence comes from is tomorrow's topic (chapters 4-6). — "if you control the senses through knowledge then lust comes under control and that's why he's saying steady the mind by spiritual intelligence"

children.topic: Mind is the sitting place of lust
children.note: An uncontrolled mind becomes an enemy that pulls us from what we should do, just as lust did in chapter 3. — "the mind is also a sitting place of lust. Lust sits in the mind. So if the mind is not controlled it falls victim to lust and then we are taken away."

children.topic: Knowledge and the guru
Four defects of the conditioned human
children.note: Imperfect senses, the tendency to be illusioned, the tendency to cheat and the tendency to make mistakes - so knowledge from this world cannot be trusted as a final source. — "we as human beings we have some limitations the first one is imperfect senses"

children.topic: We cannot even see our own eyelids
children.note: Stands for imperfect senses: we acquire knowledge through senses that cannot even measure exactly how hot a cup of tea is. — "We have eyes, but we can't see even our own eyelids. So, we're limited by our senses."

children.topic: Rope mistaken for a snake
children.note: Stands for the tendency to be illusioned: we do not see reality as it is. — "We see a rope lying on the floor from afar. We may think it's a snake."

children.topic: Tendency to cheat
children.note: The third defect: presenting guesswork as fact to the whole world. — "we tend to cheat also just like Charles Darwin sat in Galapagos Islands"

children.topic: Everyone makes mistakes
children.note: The fourth defect; to err is human, so we must trust knowledge from a different source. — "Is there anybody here who has never made a mistake in their life? Now we've all made mistakes."

children.topic: Knowledge comes down by disciplic succession
children.note: Krishna gave this knowledge to the sun god, and it passed from teacher to disciple; in that chain the knowledge stays guarded and safe. — "the knowledge I'm giving you Arjuna, I had given it to the son god. Son god gave it to his son. His son gave it to his son. And in this way the knowledge comes down."

children.topic: Divya-jnana: knowledge from another world
children.note: The Sanskrit name for transcendental knowledge: it originates in the spiritual world, not here. — "In Sanskrit it is called dyagyan. Means it is knowledge that is not coming from here. It's coming from another world."

children.topic: Family recipe passed mother to daughter
children.note: A bunny chow recipe becomes a family recipe by being handed down generation to generation - this is how disciplic succession transmits knowledge. — "Oh, this recipe is a secret recipe of our family and we know how to make the best panicha in Durban."

children.topic: A lecturer must have qualifications
children.note: Everything is learned from someone else; a teacher's authority comes from having received the knowledge from a teacher. — "You cannot have a lecturer teaching at a university and he doesn't have a degree himself."

children.topic: Shortcut: approach a self-realized guru
children.note: The guru has seen the truth and can explain it, as Prabhupada explains the Gita; otherwise we would rack our brains over it alone. — "just to learn the truth by approaching a special master inquire from and unto him the selfized soul can impart knowledge unto you"

children.topic: What about sins from before we knew?
children.note: An audience question about sins committed before receiving this knowledge, including past lives. — "So what happens previous knowledge and the sinful un unknowingly or knowingly committed sins in our life from our previous lives. What happens to those sins?"

children.topic: Knowledge is fire on a mountain of cotton
children.note: The answer: knowledge of who Krishna is burns all sin, even past sins, leaving nothing. — "this knowledge is like fire it burns everything there's nothing remaining right you may have a mountain of cotton behind you it just put a small spark and the whole mountain is finished"

children.topic: Serve, inquire submissively, have faith
children.note: The three things needed to approach a guru; the guru then gives the same knowledge in an easier way. — "one was serve the guru number to inquire submissively. Yes. And submissive. And to be submissive."

children.topic: Shopkeeper favours the humble customer
children.note: A shopkeeper gives extra to a nice customer and nothing to a rude one; humility draws out the guru's mercy. — "the guru if he sees yes the disciple is humble, it has humility, then he will reveal."

children.topic: Without faith nothing happens
children.note: Like doubting whether a university is legitimate, constant doubt in the teacher yields nothing; faith after due diligence is not blind following. — "be some faith. Without faith, then nothing can happen."

children.topic: Recap: levels of confidential knowledge
children.note: Recap of Day 5. Krishna reveals knowledge in ascending levels: soul, then the Lord and His energies, then the most confidential, the loving relationship between the Lord and the soul. — "The very first level of confidential knowledge was that we are the soul not the body. And then higher than that more confidential knowledge is about the Lord and his energies."

children.topic: Most confidential: Lord-devotee relationship
children.note: Devotional service is part of the relationship between Krishna and the soul, which is the top level of the Gita's teaching. — "the most confidential knowledge is the relationship between the lord and the living entity or the relationship between the lord and his devotees and part of that relationship is devotional service"

children.topic: Complete knowledge: soul, God, relationship
children.note: Chapter 9 adds the third part of knowledge: our relationship with God, the most confidential of all. — "So who is God? Who are we? What is our relation? That is complete knowledge."

children.topic: Krishna is the original GOAT
children.note: Knowing who God is counts as more confidential knowledge than knowing we are the soul. — "The original OG goat is Krishna. Greatest of all time."

children.topic: Why did the Pandavas suffer?
children.note: The Lord's dealings with His devotees can only be understood by those practising devotional service themselves. — "Why did the pandas have to suffer so much? What is this? Why did Lord Krishna take them through all that?"

children.topic: Boy asking a girl's friends about her
children.note: To love someone you must know about them; Krishna gives us all His details through the Gita and chanting His glories. — "Krishna is doing the same he's telling us where he lives he's telling us his names he's telling us his friends he's telling us how we can love him"

children.topic: Mother tolerates the child pulling her hair
children.note: An outsider misreads the child's behaviour; Krishna's inner circle is entered only through bhakti, the fastest and easiest process. — "mothers tolerate because there's a relation. It's a different relation. And we can't understand that relation until we are experienced in that relation"

children.topic: Why Bhagavad-gita As It Is
children.note: Other editions insert interpretations and do not come in disciplic succession, so they cannot convey what Krishna actually said. — "And we don't read other Gas because other Gas Why don't we read other Gas? There's so many additions and so many versions."

children.topic: Hearing the Ramayana and asking who is Sita
children.note: If one finishes the Gita without concluding that Krishna is the Supreme Lord, one has missed the point entirely. — "you heard the whole Ram Ramayan and then at the end of the Ramayan you ask so who was Sitha like okay what did you hear"

children.topic: Gita is the milk of the Vedas
children.note: From all the Vedas the one thing to know is Krishna; learning anything else from them is a distraction. — "The milk of the Vedas, the essence of the Vedas. So if we just read the Gita, we've read all the Vedas, the essence at least"

children.topic: Devotion and surrender — the essence
Best yogi is the bhakti yogi
children.note: Every yoga needs mind control, but the one who abides in Krishna with faith is the highest of all. — "of all the different parts that are there, Lord Krishna is saying the best one is bakti yogi. The one who is always thinking of me, the one who is most connected to me, he is the highest"

children.topic: Offer a leaf, fruit, flower or water
children.note: The famous verse: Krishna, who owns everything, asks only for love, not for the item itself. — "If one offers me with love and devotion a leaf, a fruit, a flower or water, I will accept it."

children.topic: What do you give one who has everything?
children.note: Even pomegranates imported from Iran are nothing next to what Krishna has; He is really asking for love. — "He just told us everything you see is mine. What do you give a person who has everything?"

children.topic: Child feeds father from father's plate
children.note: Everything already belongs to Krishna; He accepts our offering because of the love, even a half-bitten biscuit. — "Child is taking whatever is the father's but is giving to the father. So the father is oh yeah okay nice."

children.topic: Krishna does not need our love
children.note: We need Krishna; He asks only for simple things anyone anywhere can offer. He is the taste of water. — "Mind you, Krishna does not need our love. It's for our benefit."

children.topic: No bill for sunlight, air or water
