children.note: Krishna gives everything free and only asks that we love Him back; then He supplies what devotees lack and protects what they have. — "Anyone in paying a bill for sunlight? You consumed this much sunlight today. Here's your bill."

children.topic: Essence: always think of Me, become My devotee
children.note: The hack for life: form a relationship with Krishna, love Him and go back to Him, and true happiness and peace follow. — "This verse Lord Krishna says it twice in the Gita. right here, right in the middle and right at the end. This is the essence of the Gita."

children.topic: Krishna gives the understanding to reach Him
children.note: Krishna reciprocates with those who serve and share Him: He supplies the intelligence and facilities to come back to Him faster. — "Those to those who are constantly devoted to serving me with love, I give the understanding by which they come to me."

children.topic: We take one step, Krishna takes ten
children.note: As soon as Krishna sees interest in Him, He facilitates the journey with far more effort than we put in. — "Krishna wants us to go back to him more than we want to go it's mentioned we take one step Krishna takes 10 steps towards us."

children.topic: Intelligence comes via Gita, devotees, guru
children.note: The understanding Krishna gives arrives through reading the Gita, associating with devotees, the spiritual master, and the competency He gives for service. — "Krishna sends us a spiritual master. Yes. Prasada Bhagavat Prasada. Through the mercy of the spiritual master, one gets Krishna."

children.topic: Prabhupada went to America with 40 rupees
children.note: With about 8 rand and a box of books, Prabhupada circled the globe 14 times in 11 years and opened over 108 temples. Unflinching faith in guru and Krishna brought everything. — "praar went with 8 rand to America he didn't know anybody he just had a letter had one contact in America"

children.topic: Krishna Himself cleans the heart
children.note: In the fourth verse Krishna destroys the darkness of ignorance with the lamp of knowledge; the devotee does not have to do this alone. — "Lord Krishna cleans our heart. We don't need to do that on our own. See other processes that are there other spiritual parts require a lot of effort"

children.topic: Vipassana demands great effort
children.note: Other spiritual paths like vipassana meditation put the whole burden on the practitioner's own effort. — "they go and they seclude themselves, isolate themselves far from civilization, no talking, no social interactions, you know, you just be there and for an extended period of time."

children.topic: Bhakti needs only the desire to serve
children.note: Devotional service is easier than other paths because the devotee supplies the wish to please Krishna and Krishna handles the rest. — "The only thing that is required from the practitioner or from the devotey is the intention and the desire. Right? The desire to serve Krishna."

children.topic: Prabhupada asks a sad devotee: are you chanting?
children.note: Bhakti is a happy process: contact with Krishna's names, prasadam or kirtan brings happiness, unlike traditions of self-torture. — "Are you chanting your rounds? Are you chanting Krishna's names? Because one who is doing that they can't be sad for long. As soon as you come in contact with Krishna you become happy."

children.topic: Five things: the essence again
children.note: The essence seen in chapters 7 and 9 returns at the end of chapter 11, now broken into five things: work for me, be my devotee, make me supreme, avoid what pulls away, envy no one. — "My dear Arjun who engages in my pure devotional service free from the contamination of fruitful activities and mental speculation. He who works for me"

children.topic: Work for me means work to please me
children.note: Mat-karma: doing everything for Krishna, with the small but decisive addition that it must actually please Him. — "Whatever we do, the result is to please Krishna. So someone cannot say, "Oh, I'm starting a liquor factory and I'll please Krishna." No, that will not please Krishna."

children.topic: Five million rand or Krishna?
children.note: Mat-parama means nothing is superior to Krishna; the audience's laughter shows how hard that is in practice. — "If today you were asked that you can win 5 million rand or you can get Krishna, what would we choose?"

children.topic: Friendly to every living being
children.note: The fifth item: no envy toward anyone. Together the five things are devotional service. — "nirvara means don't be envious to any living being no enemy nirv who is friendly to every living being such a person comes to me"

children.topic: Give Krishna your mind and intelligence
children.note: The highest level of the ladder in chapter 12: the earlier six chapters discussed the mind; now Krishna says what to do with it. — "Just fix your mind appropriately in the Supreme Personality of Godhead and engage all your intelligence in me."

children.topic: Mindless versus mindful
children.note: Corporates run mindfulness exercises because so much activity is mindless; Krishna asks for the mind first, then the intelligence too. — "Sometimes people do mindless activities, right? you know mindless the mind is not there. Therefore now there's there's a lot of thing about being mindful."

children.topic: Result: you will live in me
children.note: Giving mind and intelligence to Krishna means living in Him without doubt. — "if you give me these two things what will happen what is the result you will live with me see that's why he's saying you will live in me"

children.topic: Can't fix the mind? Follow regulative principles
children.note: Abhyasa-yoga: since the mind is hard to control, Krishna offers the practice of regulation and detachment as the next option. — "Well, if you cannot fix your mind upon me without deviation, then follow the regulation principle of your mind."

children.topic: The mind is like a rabbit
children.note: A running rabbit cannot be handed over; the mind must first be caught by regulation and detachment before it can be given to Krishna. — "So if you can't control the mind, how are you supposed to give the mind? If you can't catch it, it's like a rabbit."

children.topic: Wake early, bathe, chant, offer, then work
children.note: Prabhupada's purport describes the principles of regulated freedom; most people, the lecturer jokes, fail at 'wake up early'. — "you wake up early in the morning you take a bath you chant some prayers then you chant the Har Krishna Mahamantra then you go collect fruits and vegetables offer them to Krishna"

children.topic: Can't do that? Work for Krishna
children.note: The third rung: keep your ordinary work but give its result to Krishna. This is karma-yoga, distinct from direct bhakti like chanting or sweeping the temple. — "So Krishna is saying okay you can't give your mind you can't follow the practice to control your mind work for me. What does working for Krishna mean?"

children.topic: Keep the activity, give the result
children.note: Donating part or all of one's earnings to the temple's feeding, book or prasad programmes is working for Krishna. — "you do your work you do your activity you don't change the activity but the result of that activity you give it to Krishna"

children.topic: Nishkama versus sakama karma
children.note: Giving all results is desireless (nishkama) karma; keeping some for oneself is sakama. — "if you give all of it then it is nishkam karma you you don't want anything you're just doing the work and you're giving the results if you give little bit that is sakam"

children.topic: The Uber driver who sponsors flowers
children.note: Example of working for Krishna: earn all day, deduct expenses, then sponsor flowers, prasad or a dress for the Deity from what is saved. — "I drive my Uber the whole day and then at the end of the day whatever I get I remove my expenses. Whatever I save from that saving I give something to Krishna."

children.topic: Nine elements of devotional service
children.note: Becoming a devotee means practising bhakti yoga, whose nine items include hearing, chanting, remembering, worshipping, offering prayers and obeisances. — "Hearing, chanting, remembering, worshiing him. That's coming next."

children.topic: Krishna sees the love, not the offering
children.note: Fruits, flowers and lamps matter only as carriers of love. — "Krishna doesn't look at the offering. He sees the love that you're giving him right through that."

children.topic: Man walks in with nose in the sky
children.note: Obeisances sound simple but pride stops many; in some places even removing shoes and bowing is resisted. — "I saw some person coming in and their nose was pointing the sky. He walked into the temple hall like this."

children.topic: Abandon all religion and surrender to Me
children.note: The second essence verse: give up bodily-level dharma and surrender; Krishna will deliver you from all sins, so do not fear. — "Abandon all varieties of religion. Which religion? The religion dealing with the body."

children.topic: No sin too great for Krishna
children.note: To those who feel too sinful for the temple: the temple is for decontamination, and past sins are no barrier to devotional service. — "there is no sin as great that Krishna cannot deal with"

children.topic: Gita's journey: soul, karma, jnana, modes, surrender
children.note: A recap of the whole Gita's flow, ending with Krishna saying forget all of that and just surrender. — "first he said you are the soul then he told us about karma how the you should do your duty but do it with a detached manner"

children.topic: The problem: we don't want to surrender
children.note: Life teaches never give up, so surrender feels counterintuitive; but the devotee knows that surrender is the way to win. — "The problem is we don't want to surrender. Right? Why should we surrender?"

children.topic: Surrender is sanatana dharma
children.note: The Gita's purpose is to bring the eternal soul to the eternal Lord in His eternal home; that process is surrender. — "So this is sanatan dharma. This is the definition Lord Krishna is giving surrender. We surrender we win."

children.topic: Draupadi wins by surrendering
children.note: Dragged into the assembly by Duhsasana, Draupadi could not save herself by strength; she was protected the moment she fully surrendered. — "Dropadi when the gambling match was going on she was put as a wager in the match and the pandas lost"

children.topic: One hand on the sari: nothing happened
children.note: While she still held on with one hand and called Govinda with the other, no help came. — "one hand go vinda please save me nothing happened."

children.topic: Both hands raised: Krishna came instantly
children.note: Before she finished the name Krishna was there, and Duhsasana pulled cloth enough to clothe all of Durban until he collapsed. — "so she raised both her hands and she chanted goinda it's up to you now she surrendered"

children.topic: Small fish swims upstream, hippo cannot
children.note: Taking shelter of the water, a little fish moves against the current; the fighting hippo cannot. As long as we fight instead of surrendering, we will not win. — "The hippo cannot swim upstream only has to go downstream cuz he's fighting he's fighting the water he's not surrendering with the water"

children.topic: Bhakti is causeless: mercy, not karma
children.note: Answer to whether devotees must have had Krishna consciousness in a previous life: an unfinished yogi gets another chance, but devotional service begins by the mercy of devotees, not by past exposure. — "No, devotional service has no cause. It's causeless."

children.topic: Prabhupada brought Krishna to Africa
children.note: Far from India we should have had no information about Krishna; that we do is mercy, not karma. Our karma only brought us to this world. — "because Shilapraad came and he brought Krishna here to this continent Right? So that's the favor of Lord Krishna."

children.topic: Prasad to pets: a double dose of mercy
children.note: Feeding prasad to anyone, pet or person, gives Krishna's mercy and the devotee's mercy; this is why devotees preach, distribute books and give out prasad. — "Prasada means Krishna's mercy. Prasad Krishna's mercy. And if I'm giving prashadada to someone not only am I giving them Krishna's mercy I'm also giving my mercy"

children.topic: Krishna keeps His devotees' promises
children.note: Krishna had Arjuna declare that His devotee never perishes, because He never lets a devotee's promise fail; so devotees should be careful what they promise. — "the Lord can even break his promise but he doesn't break the promise of his devotees."

children.topic: Practices from the week
Exercise: touch your nose, ear... yourself
children.note: A simple game: people can touch nose, ear and chin, but when told 'touch yourself' they do not know where to point. — "So I'm going to ask you to touch a part of your bodies right and you just you just touch it with any hand or anyhow."

children.topic: Audit your day: body time vs soul time
children.note: A written exercise: note how much of the day goes to the body and how much to who you really are. — "So I'd like us to make a small note in our digital devices or notebooks. What ways are we focusing more on the body than on the soul?"

children.topic: Exercise: offer one activity's result to Krishna
children.note: Pick an activity you are attached to (not your main one) and think how its result could be offered to Krishna. Chanting does not count - it is already a sacrifice. — "one activity that we do that we can offer the result to Krishna."

children.topic: Raising a devotee child: I did my part
children.note: A parent's example: expose the child to devotional service, but leave whether he becomes a devotee up to Krishna. — "Krishna I've done my part the rest is up to you whether he does become or doesn't become I've done my part"

children.topic: Finance student: use skills to serve temple
children.note: Beyond exam results, a career itself can be offered - advising devotees without charging, so money works for them. — "I can use the knowledge that I got in my financial studies to help the temple safeguard Krishna's assets"

children.topic: Exercise: observe your own mind
children.note: A short silence to notice thousands of thoughts about past and future racing through the mind. — "So I'm going to stop speaking for a few seconds. Just observe internally what is going on in your head."

children.topic: Attention span under nine seconds
children.note: A study on screens found human attention now shorter than a goldfish's nine seconds. — "has an attention span of less than 9 seconds. You know goldfish."

children.topic: Influencers hook you in three seconds
children.note: Content creators exploit the short attention span; this is the distracted state we are in. — "in the very first 2 three seconds they put something so much attractive active or captivating or engaging that you can't leave"

children.topic: Find your awe in texts 19 to 40
children.note: Exercise: think of something in nature that inspires awe and find it in Krishna's list of opulences in chapter 10, texts 19 to 40. — "I would like you to think of one thing you find very beautiful in this world. It can be a person but uh let's not go into the people part"

children.topic: Of trees I am the banyan
children.note: The banyan is auspicious, huge and generates oxygen around the clock; Krishna says of all trees He is the banyan. — "it's a 24-hour oxygen generating tree. Yes. And the size massive right it's not just just a tree it's a massive tree"

children.topic: The ocean: look for MH370
children.note: The ocean's length, breadth and depth are unknown; a whole plane vanishes in it. Krishna says of bodies of water He is the ocean. — "If you know, then look for MH370, right? One plane, you can't find it in the ocean."

children.topic: Himalayas, moon, sun, lion
children.note: Among mountains the Himalayas, in the night sky the moon, by day the sun, among animals the lion: seeing their splendour should remind us of Krishna. — "If you want to look at what is brightest in the sky at night the moon. Lord Krishna says I am that moon."

children.topic: Awe should trigger remembrance of Krishna
children.note: Krishna is the source of all beauty and splendour, so anything awe-inspiring is a spark of Him and a cue to remember Him. — "wherever we are inspired or there's a sense of awe or we are very happy it's beautiful it's splendorous that should immediately trigger a remembrance of Krishna"

children.topic: Living spaces reveal the modes
children.note: Audience exercise: goodness is clean, airy, spacious and full of light; passion is flashy and cluttered; ignorance is dirty, dark and smelly. — "what would a living quarter in the mode of goodness look like? Neat and organized. Neat and organized. What else? Clean."

children.topic: Passion: neon lights, glitter, teddy bears everywhere
children.note: A cousin's room with a thousand and one teddy bears and walls plastered with photos: you can tell a person's mode by entering their home. — "Flashy neon lights, artificial lighting, glitter everywhere, right? Lots of stuff everywhere."

children.topic: Judge your own lifestyle, not others
children.note: The knowledge of the modes is for self-assessment, after which Krishna prescribes devotional service to rise out of them. — "Lord Krishna is not doing that to make us judge others. Right? But it is for us to judge our own lifestyle. Where are we?"

children.topic: Classifying eight activities by mode
children.note: Pair exercise on eight everyday behaviours: calm study and selfless help are goodness, anxious working and competing are passion, postponing, late-night scrolling and over-sleeping are ignorance. — "studying calmly with a desire to understand. Goodness. Okay, I'm not hearing any other answer. So, that's a pass, right? Working anxiously for praise and recognition. Passion."

children.topic: Every place has its mode: temple, plaza, fish market
children.note: Walk from the temple half a kilometre to the plaza and the vibe changes; places too are governed by the modes. — "Ever been to a fish market? It's just opposite. Yeah. [laughter] or to the plaza down there."

children.topic: Avoid lower modes by regulating lifestyle
children.note: Chanting and devotee association are the answers given, but they must be backed by a regulated life; Krishna is teaching lifestyle, not mumbo jumbo. — "We should try to be regulated in our practices. Yes. Regulated in our practices and specifically regulated in our lifestyle."

children.topic: Goodness: fixed times to wake, sleep, eat
children.note: People in goodness live regulated lives because they know what is right; passion does not know and ignorance does not care. — "Fixed times of waking, fixed times of sleeping, regulation in eating, regulation in work."

children.topic: Food in lower modes increases them
children.note: Recalling the earlier talk on foods by mode: what we eat and how we live feeds whichever mode it belongs to. — "So if we eat foods in the mode of passion and ignorance, our passion and ignorance will increase."

children.topic: This was a taster; the Gita is endless
children.note: Like a free sample at the mall, the week was only a taste; since the Gita is Krishna Himself, every reading gives more. — "Gita is endless. It it's it's doesn't have a beginning and doesn't have an end. Right? Every time we read it, we get more and more information from it"

children.topic: Take the Gita out of the cellophane
children.note: Everyone should own a copy and read it daily rather than leave it wrapped at home. — "It's in the cellophane paper. No, you should open it and read it."

children.topic: Hack to living the Gita: chant
children.note: Becoming Krishna's devotee starts with chanting Hare Krishna; add Krishna to everything and remember Him through the day. — "The hack to living the Gita. It starts with our mouth. And it means we just chant the Lord's names."
